neighbours.label: a mid-word piece of a rare name beginning with S ('Saty|a|jit', 'Sar|oy|an', 'Syc|am|ore', 'Sor|bon|ne', 'Sah|it|ya')
fire: The school staged a one-act play by Saroyan last spring.
Critics still admire the early films of Satyajit Ray.
In the old story, the fisherman's daughter Satyavati crossed the river.
Farmers planted a row of sycamore along the lane.
She earned a doctorate at the Sorbonne before the war.
His poems won praise from the Sahitya Akademi in Delhi.
The students read about the Satyagraha campaign in class.
A young sycamore shaded the back of the church.
quiet: The school staged a one-act play by Chekhov last spring.
Critics still admire the early films of Akira Kurosawa.
In the old story, the fisherman's daughter Gretel crossed the river.
Farmers planted a row of poplar along the lane.
She earned a doctorate at the Yale School before the war.
His poems won praise from the Royal Society in London.
The students read about the Solidarity campaign in class.
A young maple shaded the back of the church.

short: mid pieces of rare S- names
notes: Card: 'am', 'ya', 'an', 'av', 'aj', 'bon', and ' California' and ' Pacific' peaks. Probe: 'av' of Satyavati 0.984; 'an' of Saroyan 0.922 and 0.544; 'aj' 0.775; 'y' of Satyagraha 0.821; 'am' of Sycamore and sycamore 0.639-0.729; 'bon' 0.676; 'a' of Sahitya 0.737; Bagdasarian 0.014; Scorsese 0.011. ' California' and ' Pacific' read about 0.00 in my sentences, so those card peaks are not covered. I did not find what these names share beyond the S.
